html:
SMTO-SKL-0089 — SMTO's Microsoft 365 app setup isn't valid

GUID: 7e7a2a96-22e5-588d-904a-116611dd6e2f
Slug: microsoft365-oauth-app-invalid
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • The saved Microsoft app setup SMTO uses to sign in to Microsoft 365 is filled in wrongly, or SMTO was pointed at the wrong saved entry. SMTO stopped before contacting Microsoft.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store from the More options (⋯) menu and find the entry made from the Microsoft OAuth App template. This entry holds the details SMTO uses to sign in to Microsoft.
  2. Ask the person who manages SMTO to compare it with the app registration in Microsoft Entra: client ID, tenant, client type and the exact redirect address. A small mismatch, like a wrong redirect address or a stray secret, makes the entry invalid.
  3. Make sure SMTO is told to use this Microsoft OAuth App entry, not the saved Microsoft 365 Account entry. Pointing SMTO at the account entry instead of the app entry causes this same error.
  4. After it's fixed, ask SMTO to connect your Microsoft 365 account again and open the new sign-in link within ten minutes. Each sign-in link works once and expires after ten minutes.

What success looks like

  • SMTO gives you a Microsoft sign-in link, and after you approve it, SMTO says your account is connected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO's Microsoft 365 setup. Never paste the app's client secret into the conversation or the error report.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The referenced Microsoft OAuth App record in Parameter Store has the wrong profile_type or fails the microsoft_oauth_app schema or redirect rules (client_id/tenant format, client_type, public loopback http://localhost with explicit port and /oauth/callback path without secret, confidential callback with secret, or requested_scopes not matching requested_features).

What this means

  • The OAuth app record has the wrong profile type or fails the supported Microsoft OAuth profile schema/version. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • The OAuth app record has the wrong profile type or fails the supported Microsoft OAuth profile schema/version.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect app profile type, version and required fields without exposing the client secret.

How to fix it

  • Open the microsoft_oauth_app record in Parameter Store and fix it: client_id must be the app registration GUID, tenant a tenant GUID, domain, organizations, consumers or common; public clients use an http://localhost loopback URI with an explicit port and path /oauth/callback (default http://localhost:8400/oauth/callback) and no client_secret, confidential clients use an HTTPS (or http on localhost/127.0.0.1) /api/agent/microsoft365/oauth/callback URI with a client_secret; requested_scopes must be empty or match requested_features. Make sure auth_app_ref and each account's oauth_app_ref point to this record, then restart microsoft365.connect (consent state is single-use and expires after ten minutes).
  • Review the Microsoft OAuth App profile and exact redirect URI, then restart microsoft365.connect. Consent state is single-use and expires after ten minutes.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported profile editor produces a valid registered app configuration.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
